subject: Request: emergency revert for delta-3.2c after sustained p95 degradation
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena@brightedge.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: sudden p95 spike since 08:55 - delta-3.2c

Hi Mateo,

We started seeing a sustained p95 latency spike across our traffic at ~08:55 PST after you rolled delta-3.2c (all US traffic). p50 looks fine but p95 jumped from ~320ms to ~1.9s and it's impacting our interactive editor flows. I attached the SLO report and a short traces snapshot.

Is there an immediate rollback or fallback you can do? This is affecting our customers and we need ETA/plan.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Director of Product, BrightEdge
Lena Ortiz | lena@brightedge.ai

Attachments: brightedge_slo-report.pdf, traces_0800-0910.txt (see attached)
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@brightedge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden p95 spike since 08:55 - delta-3.2c

Hi Lena — thanks for the signal and the artifacts. I'm looking into this with SE/Infra now. Initial telemetry shows the spike aligns with the delta-3.2c rollout at 08:42 (canary -> full).

Short answer: we can perform an emergency revert to the previously pinned variant (delta-3.1b) if you want immediate mitigation. Before I proceed I want to confirm BrightEdge is comfortable with a regional canary revert (US-EAST first) and customer-facing notice.

Ben, Kim, Monica — tagging for triage and approval to execute a revert. Ben, can you confirm whether the quantization path we changed in 3.2c is the likely root cause and the estimated service impact of a revert (token-cost/latency delta)?

I'll prepare the rollback runbook and a short customer notice once I have sign-off.

— Mateo
Staff Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: delta-3.2c_p95-graphs.png (attached)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden p95 spike since 08:55 - delta-3.2c

On Tue, Apr 27, 2027 at 09:25 Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Ben, can you confirm whether the quantization path we changed in 3.2c is the likely root cause...

Quick summary from infra diagnostics:
- Telemetry: p95 uplift co-located with a microcode-level kernel path that was switched in delta-3.2c for INT8 streaming. Heap/GC are normal, CPU saturation is moderate on affected hosts.
- Repro: We can reproduce a small p95 bump locally with the 3.2c quant path on a representative prompt set (editor-heavy).
- Suggested mitigation: revert variant to delta-3.1b across US-EAST canary (10% traffic) and monitor for 30m; if stable, roll to 100%. Revert risk: ~0.8% cost increase due to fallback to a higher-precision path, but p95 expected to return near baseline.

If leadership approves, infra can schedule the canary revert now (ETA 25–40m to start canary; 60–90m for full roll). We should also open a short SLA carveout notice to the account and record the incident for RCA.

Ben
Principal Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Lena Ortiz <lena@brightedge.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Approval request: emergency canary revert (delta-3.2c -> delta-3.1b) for BrightEdge (DEAL-8421)

Kim — requesting approval to execute an emergency canary revert for BrightEdge. Summary: delta-3.2c rollout at 08:42 correlates with a p95 latency increase to ~1.9s for BrightEdge traffic. Ben's diagnostic points to the new INT8 streaming kernel path as the likely cause.

Proposed action:
- Step 1: Start canary revert (US-EAST) at 10:30 -> 10% traffic to delta-3.1b
- Step 2: Monitor p95, error rates, and customer traces for 30 min
- Step 3: If stable, promote to 100% over the next 45–90 min

Risks & mitigations:
- Expected cost delta: +~0.8% token cost (temporary)
- User impact risk: reverting during business hours lowers p95 and customer complaints; canary minimizes blast radius
- Audit: we'll create a short SLA carveout entry and an incident ticket that BrightEdge can reference (RCA to follow)

Attachments: rollback playbook link (https://app.redwood.ai/rollouts/rollout-9923) and the graph snapshot I sent earlier.

Please reply with "APPROVE" or "DECLINE". If I don't hear back within 20 minutes I'll escalate to ops on-call as per emergency policy.

Thanks,
Mateo
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Lena Ortiz <lena@brightedge.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Approval request: emergency canary revert (delta-3.2c -> delta-3.1b) for BrightEdge (DEAL-8421)

APPROVE (provisional). Conditions:
- Start with US-EAST 10% canary only.
- Notify BrightEdge of the canary start and expected timeline (please use the draft notice Mateo prepared).
- Create a short SLA carveout note with legal and CS copied — Monica, please create the entry and notify BrightEdge.
- Engineering (Ben/Dylan): pray that full revert metrics match expected; if errors spike, stop the revert immediately and notify leadership.

Mateo — proceed with canary revert and update thread every 15m during the canary window.
